title: Input Tax Credit
outcomes: Apply eligibility conditions and time limits for ITC.
Apportion common credit under rules 42 and 43.
Apply ITC in special circumstances and ISD rules.

meta.exam_tip: Strip blocked and exclusive credits first; apportion only the common pool.

concepts.title: Eligibility and conditions for ITC
body: Section 16(1) allows a registered person to take credit of tax charged on inward supplies that serve, or are meant to serve, its business. Section 16(2) conditions: possession of a tax invoice or debit note; the details furnished by the supplier and appearing in GSTR-2B; receipt of goods or services (including bill-to-ship-to and delivery to agents); tax actually paid by the supplier; and the recipient having filed its return.

Payment must be made to the supplier within 180 days of the invoice; otherwise the ITC is reversed with interest and re-availed on payment (RCM, deemed supplies without consideration excluded). Goods received in lots: credit on the last lot. ITC is not available on tax component if depreciation is claimed on it.

Section 16(4): ITC for a financial year must be taken by 30 November of the next year or the annual return date, whichever earlier (with specific relaxations for earlier years and revocation cases). Rule 86B restricts use of credit to 99% of output tax for certain high-value taxpayers.
concepts.analogy: Invoice, 2B, receipt, tax paid, return filed — and pay within 180 days.
concepts.work: An invoice for October 2026 must be claimed by 30 November 2027.

concepts.title: Blocked credits
body: Section 17(5) blocks credit on: motor vehicles for transport of persons with seating up to 13 (unless used for further supply, passenger transport, driving training, or transport of goods), and their repair, insurance and servicing; vessels and aircraft (with exceptions); eatables and drinks, catering, beauty and health services, cosmetic and plastic surgery, life and health cover, club and fitness memberships, and leave or home travel for staff — unless obligatory for employers under law or used for the same category of outward supply.

Also blocked: works contract services and inputs used to build immovable property on own account (plant and machinery apart), even when used in business; composition tax; goods or services received by non-residents (except imports); goods or services for personal consumption; goods lost, stolen, destroyed, written off or gifted; tax paid under sections 74, 129 and 130.
"Plant and machinery" includes foundations and structural supports but excludes land, buildings, civil structures, telecom towers and pipelines laid outside factory premises.
concepts.analogy: Personal-type and construction expenses are blocked.
concepts.work: GST on a car for directors is blocked; on a goods truck it is allowed.

concepts.title: Apportionment of common credit
body: Section 17(1) and (2) restrict credit to the extent of business use and taxable (including zero-rated) supplies. Rule 42 apportions common input and input service credit monthly: remove credits for non-business (T1), exempt (T2) and blocked (T3) items; the remainder C1 less exclusive taxable credit (M) gives common credit C2; then D1 = (exempt turnover ÷ total turnover) × C2 and D2 = 5% of C2 are reversed.

Rule 43 apportions ITC on capital goods: credit on goods used exclusively for exempt or non-business purposes is not taken; for common capital goods, credit is spread over 60 months (5% per quarter) and the share attributable to exempt supplies reversed monthly.

Final reversal is computed for the whole year by the due date of the September return, with interest on excess claimed. Exempt supplies include specified transactions such as securities (1% of value) and land (value as stamp duty).
concepts.analogy: Common credit is shared by turnover ratio, with 5% deemed non-business.
concepts.work: With 20% exempt turnover, ₹4 lakh of common credit yields ₹3 lakh eligible.

concepts.title: ITC in special circumstances and ISD
body: Section 18: credit on stock and capital goods on new registration (within 30 days), on switching from composition to regular scheme, or when exempt supplies become taxable. On switching to composition or supplies becoming exempt, credit on stock is reversed. On sale of capital goods, tax payable is the higher of ITC taken less 5% per quarter and tax on transaction value.

Section 20: an Input Service Distributor must distribute credit of common input services (including RCM services from 1 April 2025) to units in the ratio of turnover, through ISD invoices, in the same month; excess distribution is recoverable with interest.
Section 41 and rule 37: credit is availed self-assessed; non-payment of supplier dues within 180 days, or mismatches, lead to reversal.
concepts.analogy: Credit follows registration changes, transfers and distribution.
concepts.work: A newly registered dealer can claim ITC on stock held on the day before registration.

illustrations.title: Rule 42 apportionment
illustrations.q: Indira Foods Ltd has total ITC of ₹10,00,000 for a month: exclusively for non-business ₹50,000; exclusively for exempt supplies ₹1,00,000; blocked under section 17(5) ₹50,000; exclusively for taxable supplies ₹4,00,000; the rest is common. Exempt turnover is ₹20 crore out of total turnover of ₹100 crore. Compute eligible ITC.

jobs.title: ITC reconciliation
jobs.situation: A company with exempt and taxable supplies prepares its monthly return.
jobs.takeaway: Credit errors often surface only in audit — reconcile monthly.

mcqs.q: Payment to the supplier must be made within how many days of invoice to retain ITC?
mcqs.explain: Second proviso to section 16(2). In practice: reverse with interest.

mcqs.q: ITC for 2026-27 must be availed by the earlier of the annual return date and:
ITC on a motor car with seating up to thirteen used by directors is:
mcqs.explain: Section 17(5)(a). In practice: exceptions for specified uses.

mcqs.q: ITC on works contract for constructing a factory building is:
mcqs.explain: Section 17(5)(c). In practice: plant and machinery excepted.

mcqs.q: Under rule 42, the deemed non-business portion of common credit is:
Capital goods credit under rule 43 is spread over:
mcqs.explain: Useful life. In practice: 5% per quarter.

mcqs.q: On new registration, ITC on stock can be claimed if application is made within:
mcqs.explain: Section 18(1)(a). In practice: stock held day before.

mcqs.q: Rule 86B restricts use of ITC for output tax to:
mcqs.explain: High-value taxpayers. In practice: exceptions apply.

viva.q: Can ITC be taken without the invoice appearing in GSTR-2B?
viva.model: It is barred: the supplier's details must appear in GSTR-2B under section 16(2)(aa).

viva.q: When is ITC on food and beverages allowed?
viva.model: When provision to employees is obligatory under a law, or when used for making an outward supply of the same category.

viva.q: What happens when capital goods with ITC are sold?
viva.model: Tax payable is the higher of ITC taken less 5% per quarter of use and tax on the transaction value.

viva.q: How does an ISD distribute credit?
viva.model: To units using the services, in the ratio of their turnover, through ISD invoices in the same month.

viva.q: Can depreciation be claimed on the GST component along with ITC?
viva.model: ITC is denied on the tax portion if depreciation is claimed on it.

cases.title: Late payment to supplier
cases.case: Rana Textiles took ITC of ₹54,000 on a supplier invoice dated 1 April 2026 for ₹3,00,000 plus GST. By 1 October 2026 it had not paid the supplier. It pays in full on 15 December 2026.

mcqs.q: ITC to be reversed after 180 days (₹):
mcqs.explain: Unpaid in full. In practice: next return.

mcqs.q: Is interest payable on the reversal?
mcqs.explain: Section 50. In practice: from date of availment.

mcqs.q: Can ITC be re-availed after payment on 15 December?
mcqs.explain: Third proviso to section 16(2). In practice: subject to time limit.

mcqs.q: Days in the 180-day window from 1 April 2026:
mcqs.explain: Statutory period. In practice: track ageing.
